entry.title: "Don’t Think About It": Why the Brain Thinks the Opposite (Bite-size Article)
entry.summary:
Introduction
Have you ever noticed that when someone tells you “don’t think about it”, you end up thinking about it even more? In the 1980s, psychologist Daniel Wegner conducted a famous experiment in which participants were told “try not to think of a white bear.” Ironically, this led them to imagine white bears even more often. This paradoxical phenomenon—where trying to suppress a thought makes it more persistent—is known as the Ironic Process Theory.
The Ironic Process Theory, proposed by Daniel Wegner, describes how attempts to suppress thoughts can actually make them stronger. Our brains employ two processes when we try not to think about something: Suppression System: the conscious effort to avoid the thought Monitoring System: the unconscious mechanism that checks whether the th…
